How fast is the process?

Amit Soman spent years building 1Source into a differentiated print, signage, and visual communications business, growing through acquisition. When he decided to sell, he hired OffDeal over M&A brokers and other investment banks.
B2B Printing

Amit was an experienced acquirer whose instinct was to write his own CIM, build his own data room, and take the meetings himself. But running two other companies, he couldn’t let the sale consume him. He needed a firm that would carry out the entire process.

Having the right positioning was just as important. Marketed as a commercial printer, 1Source would land in a commoditized bucket where valuations are suppressed. Capturing its real value meant reaching a specific set of buyers with actual operating or investing experience in visual communications, not just a checkbook: the kind a limited, self‑run process would never surface.

OffDeal repositioned the business. 1Source was not a commodity printer but a broad visual communications platform: large and grand format production, ADA and architectural signage, in‑house manufacturing, repeat B2B customers, and a record of growth through acquisition.

Amit arrived with six potential acquirers of his own and a short list of local competitors never to approach. OffDeal honored the do‑not‑contact list and built out roughly 90 buyers specific to the business, half private equity firms and their platforms, and half independent strategic operators in print and signage.

Leading buyers framed the transition around an all‑or‑nothing contingent seller note tied to performance Amit wouldn’t control after stepping back. OffDeal pushed back on the binary construct, proposed structures that scaled rather than “cliffed,” and brought rollover equity into the conversation. OffDeal introduced real ownership in the combined platform, something Amit had never considered.

After a rigorous marketing process, Amit received six competitive offers. Not one came from the buyers he had brought to OffDeal. Every offer came from a buyer OffDeal surfaced, including Banner Capital, whose Vision Graphics platform acquired the business.
B2B Printing & Signage
Stephen and Mariela Barnes hired OffDeal over the brokers and school chains that had approached them. Seven months later they sold to the buyer they chose, with the full price paid at closing.

Stephen and Mariela were ready to move on. Their daughter was leaving for college, and Mariela wanted more time with aging parents in Chile. The school ran smoothly without them, and they wanted to hand it to someone who would preserve what they had built.

Chains tended to force their own model onto a school, but this was a premium, bilingual program that families chose specifically because it was different. Stephen went looking for a better option, and found OffDeal.

The first offer looked fine on paper, but only about a fifth of the price would be paid at closing. The rest would trickle in over seven years with no interest. OffDeal pushed for the school to be valued on everything it earned for its owners, and for buyers to use an SBA loan to pay the founders up front instead of asking them to wait.
As OffDeal created a competitive auction among several buyers, the offers improved quickly. Within weeks, one bidder with SBA approval was ready to pay nearly the entire price in cash at closing.

The founders signed the LOI in early May, and the deal closed on Sept 17, 2025. The full price was paid in cash at closing, compared with about a fifth in the first offer. When the buyers’ SBA loan took longer than expected, OffDeal and the founders’ attorney kept the deal moving until it closed.

OffDeal is an AI-native investment bank for small businesses. Their AI technology automates most of the grunt work typically done by analysts at larger Wall Street banks, enabling their in-house M&A advisors to focus more on strategic client interactions, leading to faster deal closures and higher sale prices.

OffDeal was born from personal experience. In 2019, co-founder Ori E., a former banker, tried to buy a local cooking oil collection business. He was shocked by how painful, clunky, and inefficient the SMB M&A process was, with both sellers and buyers receiving little guidance. Inspired to change this, Ori partnered with Alston L. to build OffDeal.
